news.title: ‘Thought it was joke’: Ex-Belgium coach on Balogun’s World Cup red card reversal
news.lede: Rudi Garcia, who managed Belgium in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, opened up in a recent interview about USA striker Folarin Balogun’s red card being rescinded ahead of the Round of 16 match. During USA’s 2-0 win against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Round of 32, the Monaco forward committed a foul on Bosnian defender Tarik Muharemovic, for which he was sent off. Under normal circumstances, it would have ruled him out of the match against Belgium. But the involvement of US president Donald Trump provided a big assist for him as the ban was lifted by the FIFA Committee.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Japan's Sakamoto secures last-gasp 3-2 friendly win over Brazil
news.lede: Nov 14 (Reuters) - Japan's Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored ⁠a stoppage-time goal to snatch a 3-2 friendly win over Brazil in Singapore on Saturday, ⁠avenging their World Cup defeat despite Vinicius Jr's double. Hajime Moriyasu's side stunned Brazil early, ‌capitalising on defensive lapses to take a two-goal lead inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinicius ignited Brazil's comeback with a stunning strike in the 33nd minute, collecting the ball outside the penalty area and unleashing an unstoppable shot into ​the top corner. The Real Madrid winger equalised in the 75th minute ⁠when he latched onto a Bruno Guimaraes ⁠pass following a corner, skipped past his marker and curled an effort in off the post.

news.title: Football: Sakamoto goal sends Japan past Brazil for 2nd straight friendly
news.lede: SINGAPORE - Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored a late winner as Japan seized a 3-2 victory over Brazil on Saturday, their second straight international friendly success over the South Americans by the same scoreline. First-half goals from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura were cancelled out by two wonder strikes from Vinicius Jr. at Singapore National Stadium, but Coventry man Sakamoto netted the winner in second-half stoppage time in manager Hajime Moriyasu's penultimate match in charge. Japan beat the record five-time World Cup winners for the first time at the senior level with a second-half comeback in October last year in Tokyo before losing 2-1 after taking the lead in the round of 32 at the World Cup in late June in Houston. "Brazil's intensity went up once we took the lead and it was all about what we could do then," Moriyasu said.

news.title: Japan’s ‘best match’ under Moriyasu as late winner downs Brazil in thrilling National Stadium clash
news.lede: Real Madrid striker Vinicius Jr (in yellow) scored twice with long-range strikes, but Japan struck in injury time. SINGAPORE – Outgoing Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu hailed his charges for producing the “best match of my eight years as head coach”, after they beat five-time world champions Brazil 3-2 in an absorbing encounter at the National Stadium on Nov 14. Moriyasu, Japan’s longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 coach Go Oiwa. But the tournament’s postponement has now sped up the 58-year-old’s departure, and the games in Singapore against Brazil, and Paraguay on Nov 17, are now his last in charge of the team.

news.title: Raphinha opens up on frustrating 2026 FIFA World Cup hamstring injury: ‘My body pays the price’
news.lede: Raphinha recently opened up on his frustrating injury concerns during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which led to reduced game time. The FC Barcelona captain claimed that it was frustrating to sit out as players dream for such moments and it would have been heartbreaking to not play. He was advised by the medical staff to change his playing style as that created frequent injury concerns for the player. However, the Brazilian forward remained firm on sticking on to his playing style as his body would eventually pay the price.

news.title: Spain vs England: Tuchel eager to end unbeaten run of FIFA World Cup and Euro winner in Madrid
news.lede: London Thomas Tuchel believes England is ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when its face the world and European champion in Madrid on Sunday. While victory offers not much more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarterfinal in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if it could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat. “It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said England manager Tuchel, whose side beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday. “I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday,” the German added.
